title: Guards that reject before the handler
summary: Implement CanActivate with Reflector metadata and apply it with UseGuards.

scenario.briefing: The catalog now has an admin-only write route. A guard returned true for every request, including anonymous ones, so the handler ran without an authorization decision.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Review an artifact and identify the concrete risks.

hints: Use this.reflector.getAllAndOverride with the handler and class.
Return true only when the route is explicitly public.
Throw ForbiddenException when the role is not admin, then apply @UseGuards(AuthGuard).

misconceptions.description: Returning true from a guard because the happy path works.
misconceptions.feedback: A guard that always allows is not an authorization check. Deny by default and allow only explicit cases.
misconceptions.testDescription: Requests without the admin role are rejected.

misconceptions.description: Constructing a service with new inside a controller.
misconceptions.feedback: That hides the dependency from Nest and from tests. Register the provider and inject it through the constructor.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Constructing a service with new hides it from Nest and from test substitutes.

misconceptions.description: Shipping a guard that allows every request.
misconceptions.feedback: A guard with no denial path does not authorize anything. The handler runs for anonymous callers, so the change is blocked.

sections.title: Guards run before the handler
sections.body: Nest evaluates a guard before the route handler. Returning true continues the request; returning false or throwing stops it with a denial.

sections.title: Reflector reads metadata
sections.body: SetMetadata attaches values to a handler or class. Reflector reads them from the execution context, which lets one guard respect a public override.

sections.title: ExecutionContext names the transport
sections.body: The context exposes the handler, the class, and the underlying request. switchToHttp gives typed access to the request for the current HTTP adapter.

steps.title: Guard an admin route
steps.prompt: Edit auth.guard.ts. Implement AuthGuard so it reads public metadata with Reflector, rejects requests without the admin role using ForbiddenException, and apply it with @UseGuards.

tests.description: The guard implements CanActivate with an execution context.
Public routes are read from handler and class metadata.
Requests without the admin role are rejected.
The guard is applied to the controller with UseGuards.

hints: Return true only when the public flag is true.
Read the HTTP request with context.switchToHttp().getRequest().
Throw ForbiddenException when the role is not admin, then apply @UseGuards(AuthGuard).

artifact.title: auth.guard.ts
artifact.caption: The guard always allows the request and the controller builds its own service.

findings.label: AuthGuard returns true for every request, so the handler is never protected.
ProductsController constructs ProductsService with new instead of injecting it.
ProductsService is missing from the module providers array.
AuthGuard correctly uses Reflector to read route metadata.

verdicts.label: Block the change until authorization and injection are fixed.
Ship it; the guard is a valid default allow policy.

steps.explanation: The guard ignores metadata and returns true for every request, so the route has no authorization. The controller constructs its service with new, and the module never registers ProductsService as a provider, so injection cannot supply it.
hints: Check whether the guard has any denying branch.
Check how ProductsService is constructed and registered.
Look for the missing providers entry.
Reject the false reflector finding and block on authorization and injection.
